text.p: Albania said on Wednesday that army chief of staff General Sheme Kosova had been dismissed and replaced by Major General Adem Copani, President Sali Berisha's personal military adviser.

A statement from the prime minister's office published in the newspaper Rilindja Demokratike said Kosova had been sacked for failing to ensure adequate security at military posts stormed and looted of their weapons by "terrorists".
The statement said Kosova's action "resulted in military installations being destroyed and a considerable quantity of weapons and ammunition being looted by terrorists".

A separate statement from the defence ministry said Kosova had been replaced by Copani. Neither said whether Kosova had been arrested. They were issued after unconfirmed reports of the sacking on Tuesday.
Albania's parliament, controlled by Berisha's Democratic Party, declared a national state of emergency on Sunday after an armed uprising in the south of the country.

Rioters stormed army and police weapons depots and seized their arms and ammunition. The embattled authorities said on Tuesday that what they call "red rebels" remained in control of the Adriatic port of Vlore and the town of Sarande.
